boards.title: Your First Weekend at Florida State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend route through central campus, its arts spaces, recreation, and recurring FSU traditions.

cards.title: Start at Landis Green
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · central campus reset
cards.notes: Use the lawn as a simple first meeting point, then choose a sidewalk heading toward your next stop instead of trying to cover campus all at once.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gathering space with paths and recognizable buildings around it.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU describes Landis Green as a historic gathering space where students relax, study, and celebrate university traditions.
cards.source_title: GCEC 2026 | Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship | Florida State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event use requires a Student Activities permit; use it as a walk-through or meet-up space when no programmed event is underway.

cards.title: Get Oriented at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 75 North Woodward Ave.
cards.notes: Pause at the building directory and pick one manageable campus resource or activity to revisit later, rather than treating the first day as a checklist.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services and gathering destination with a public building directory.
cards.evidence_claim: The FSU Student Union provides a building directory, location-specific hours, visitor parking information, and programs for the university community.
cards.access_notes: Consult the Union’s location-specific hours before visiting; the official page also links visitor parking information.

cards.title: See What’s On at MoFA
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · art-gallery stop
cards.notes: Walk through the current galleries at your own pace and save one exhibition detail or artwork to discuss over dinner with your new group.
cards.short_summary: A free public campus museum focused on exhibitions, educational programming, and art.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s Museum of Fine Arts states that it is always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | Museum of Fine Arts
cards.access_notes: Review the museum’s visitor information for current gallery details and parking guidance before you go.

cards.title: Find a Study Floor at Strozier
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 116 Honors Way
cards.notes: Take a short floor-by-floor look, then bookmark one quiet area and one group-study option so you have familiar places when classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A six-floor central-campus library with study spaces, technology, and research materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Strozier Library is located at the center of campus, has six floors including quiet areas, and offers study spaces and technology.
cards.source_title: Robert Manning Strozier Library | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s live hours before visiting; building and staffed service-desk hours can differ.

cards.title: Check the Askew Student Life Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 942 Learning Way
cards.notes: Look over the cinema and gaming calendar, then choose a future showing or drop-in activity that fits your first few weeks on campus.
cards.short_summary: A Student Union destination that hosts Student Life Cinema and gaming programming.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU identifies Askew Student Life Center as home to Student Life Cinema, gaming at the Cyber Cafe, and esports programming.
cards.source_title: Askew Student Life Center - Florida State University Calendar
cards.access_notes: Check the official calendar for current showings and activity times before making a trip.

cards.title: Take a Reflection Walk at the FSU Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · intentional slow start
cards.notes: Walk the single path from entrance to center and back, using the time to notice what felt most useful or unfamiliar during your first day.
cards.short_summary: An accessible, one-path campus reflection space designed for walking and thinking.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU says its labyrinth has one path in and out and was created as an accessible space for reflection, creativity, gratitude, and stress reduction.
cards.access_notes: Treat the labyrinth as a quiet reflection space and give other walkers room to complete their path.

cards.title: Photograph Westcott Fountain
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · historic campus landmark
cards.notes: Take a photo from the plaza and read the site’s history; keep the visit on the surrounding walkways rather than entering the fountain.
cards.short_summary: A historic fountain-and-plaza landmark at the heart of FSU’s traditional campus imagery.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Legacy Walk identifies Westcott Fountain as a joint gift from the Florida State College for Women classes of 1915 and 1917.
cards.source_title: Westcott Fountain and Plaza | FSU Legacy Walk
cards.access_notes: Enjoy the plaza from its public walkways and follow posted campus rules around the fountain.

cards.title: Pause at the Unconquered Statue
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · outside Doak Campbell Stadium
cards.notes: View the statue from its plaza and use the official context to understand how FSU presents Seminole history and university traditions respectfully.
cards.short_summary: A large campus statue near the stadium connected to FSU’s Seminole presence and traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU describes the bronze Osceola-and-horse statue as approximately 31 feet tall and notes its location in the university’s Seminole presence on campus.
cards.source_title: Seminole Presence on Campus | Florida State University
cards.access_notes: Visit the public exterior and use the university’s Seminole Tribe materials for context; event-day access patterns can differ.

cards.title: Spend the Afternoon at Lakefront Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Lake Bradford, four miles from main campus
cards.notes: Plan transport before leaving campus, then choose a low-key activity such as the beach, disc golf, or an FSU-student kayak rental if conditions allow.
cards.short_summary: A 73-acre Lake Bradford recreation site with water, beach, and outdoor game options.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Lakefront Park is a 73-acre facility on Lake Bradford offering kayaking, paddleboarding, swimming, sand volleyball, and disc golf; kayak and paddleboard rentals are free for FSU students.
cards.source_title: FSU Lakefront Park – FSU Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: The park is four miles from main campus. Check facility hours and status before traveling; alcohol and pets are not allowed.

cards.title: Close with a Flying High Circus Performance
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Haskin Circus Complex
cards.notes: If a show is scheduled, arrive at the box office about 90 minutes early with your FSU ID to request a student wristband while supplies last.
cards.short_summary: A student-run circus with reserved free-admission capacity for current FSU students at designated shows.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s Flying High Circus says current FSU students can receive free admission with valid FSU ID, with up to 400 student seats held for each Spring and Halloween series show.
cards.source_title: FSU Student Tickets FAQ | The FSU Flying High Circus
cards.access_notes: Free student wristbands are distributed at the circus box office beginning 1.5 hours before each eligible performance; availability is limited.
